_comment: Declared inventory of everything this repository publishes, and of the derived files that must agree with it. WHAT THIS GUARANTEES TODAY: nothing is generated FROM this file at runtime yet. deploy/feed-excludes.txt, .gitignore and scripts/push-to-web-host.sh are still hand-maintained and are still what the deploy and the push actually obey. All this file buys, as of C1 Phase 0, is that scripts/deploy/render-publication.sh can reproduce those three regions byte-for-byte from here, and tests/publication-registry/ fails if it ever cannot. That is a detector, not an enforcement: a hand edit to one of those three files that is NOT mirrored here turns the test red, but nothing stops the edit from being made or deployed. Turning consumers around to read this file is C1 Phase 1 and later.

kind_definitions._comment: The taxonomy is defined by ONE measurable question: can these bytes change without a commit to this repository? That question is what decides whether a sha256 pin in a signed manifest can survive, which is the only thing the kind gate acts on.
kind_definitions.stream: Content can change without any commit — host cron, runtime push, or an operator writing straight to the public tree. A pin taken at signing time goes stale on its own. MUST NOT appear in pinned_by.
kind_definitions.record: Immutable once written and addressed by its own content or by a date that never recurs, at a URL that never points at different bytes. Safe to pin.
kind_definitions.static: Changes only when a commit in this repository changes it, and is delivered by the git deploy. Safe to pin, on the condition that the commit which changes it also re-issues the pin — that condition is what scripts/check-identity-pins.sh enforces.

coverage._comment: Read this before treating this file as a source of truth for anything. It is deliberately placed above the data.
governs: .gitignore — only the '# ---- Runtime-generated site data ----' section, from that header to the line before the next '# ---- ' header
scripts/push-to-web-host.sh — only two regions: the 'Allowed targets' header comment table, and the flat-filename case pattern line

does_not_govern.surface: The rest of the tracked public/ tree (HTML pages, CSS, JS, images, fonts).
does_not_govern.measured: 149 tracked files under public/ that are neither public/api/* nor public/.well-known/* (git ls-files public/ | grep -v -E '^public/(api|\.well-known)/' | wc -l, 2026-08-07).
does_not_govern.why_excluded: They have exactly one owner (the git deploy), are never pushed, and are never pinned, so there is no lock-step obligation for a registry to hold. tests/publication-registry/ checks this claim rather than assuming it: any tracked file under public/ that is absent from publications[] must also be absent from feed-excludes and from the push allowlist. If that ever stops holding, the file has acquired a second owner and must be added here.

does_not_govern.surface: /etc/cron.d on the validator host — the cron files that actually invoke the producers.
does_not_govern.measured: Six cron basenames have a creating installer in this repo (metal-host-advance, metal-anchor-watch, metal-anchor-publish-health, metal-identity-pins, metal-host-drift, metal-watch-validators — grep of scripts/install-*.sh for cron.d/, 2026-08-07). NONE of them produces a publication listed here. Every publication whose publisher is 'push' is produced by a cron whose command body is not in this repo. That is recorded per entry as owner.cron_installer_in_repo, which is false for all of them.
does_not_govern.why_excluded: A registry cannot govern text it cannot read. The spec (§9) records that 15 project cron files run in production and 7 have no repo installer; that count was measured on the host, not by this file, and is not re-measured here. What IS measured here is the repo side: the schedule, the arguments, and the environment that decide when and where a producer writes are outside this file for every push-owned publication. Do not read owner.producer as 'the registry controls this artifact' — it means only 'this script contains the write'.

does_not_govern.surface: The web host's forced-command receive wrapper (/home/<deploy user>/bin/receive-metal-push).
does_not_govern.measured: Its flat-filename allowlist is operator-local and not in this repo. Only the subdirectory block is (scripts/deploy/receive-subdir-allowlist.snippet.sh), and tests/publication-registry/ checks that block's basename patterns against this file and against the sender.
does_not_govern.why_excluded: Adding a name here and to the sender still leaves the receiver to be changed by hand on the host. A push whose name is new here will be rejected remotely until that happens.

does_not_govern.surface: Whether anything listed here is actually reachable at its public URL right now.
does_not_govern.measured: Not measured. No HTTP request is made by this file or by its tests.
does_not_govern.why_excluded: Phase 0 is offline and hermetic by construction. Liveness is the reconciler's job (spec §9), not the registry's.

publications.note: The one asymmetric entry: excluded from the deploy's --delete, but NOT on scripts/push-to-web-host.sh's allowlist. scripts/push-to-web-host.sh (header, 'Note:') states it is delivered by a different mechanism and does not name it. This file does not know what that mechanism is; it is not in the repo.

kind=record because the member filename contains the content hash: a given URL under this prefix never resolves to different bytes. This is the shape the spec's kind discipline wants api/anchor-source.json to move to (C4).

publications.note: kind=record on the date key: a given day's snapshot is written once and never rewritten. The master copy lives in the host state dir, not in the repo — the repo path is a staging mirror.

The directory is one --delete exclude, but the push allowlist names its members individually (schedule.ics and a 16-64 hex token name), so the two push_allowlist_only entries below carry those. Member filenames embed a private token; never committed.

publications.kind_note: kind=static under the definition above (its published bytes change only when a commit changes them). Semantically it is a record — the signed pre-image of one anchor event — served at a mutable URL. The spec calls that the category error behind the 2026-07-07 stale-publication incident and assigns the fix to C4. It is NOT counted as a kind violation here because it is not pinned by anything, so no gate has anything to act on.

push_allowlist_only._comment: Names the push wrapper accepts that are not one-file publications: they are members of the calendar/ directory entry above. Kept out of publications[] so that 'one path, one row' stays true there.

known_kind_violations._comment: Acknowledgement list for the kind gate (kind=stream MUST NOT appear in any pinned_by), following the same expiry design as deploy/identity-pin-baseline.json: an entry suppresses the gate only while the violation it describes is still exactly the violation present. If the named pin disappears from public/api/identity.json's artifact_manifest, or the named path stops being kind=stream, the entry no longer applies and the test reports it as OBSOLETE — so this cannot become a permanent mute. Every entry is a C4 work item. NOT AN ALERT PATH: this gate acts on the registry's own declarations, not on live bytes. It says nothing about whether a pin currently matches; that is scripts/check-identity-pins.sh's job.

measured_against.method: jq over .artifact_manifest of public/api/identity.json; each entry contributes <key>.sha256 and, where present, <key>.schema_sha256

evidence_json.sha256.reason: Push-owned stream regenerated by scripts/gen-evidence.sh on the metal-evidence cron.

validator_json.sha256.reason: Push-owned stream rewritten by scripts/node-info.sh from live metalgo RPC.

cycle_history_jsonl.sha256.reason: Push-owned stream regenerated by scripts/gen-cycle-history.sh on the metal-cycle-history cron. Same structural class as the three above.
cycle_history_jsonl.sha256.note: This is the fourth stream pin and the only one deploy/identity-pin-baseline.json does not list. That is a documentation gap, NOT a gate gap: scripts/check-identity-pins.sh classifies it as stream from deploy/feed-excludes.txt and stream-class pins never alert there, so nothing was being suppressed. Recording it here makes all four visible in one place.

known_render_drift._comment: Places where a target file's CURRENT bytes are not what this registry would render, recorded rather than fixed because Phase 0 must not modify the target files. Same expiry design as known_kind_violations: each entry pins both what is expected and what is there, so any change to either side makes the entry stop applying and the test reports it as OBSOLETE.

push_allowlist_doc.missing_rows.evidence: Both names are enforced by the flat-filename case branch of scripts/push-to-web-host.sh, and both are in deploy/feed-excludes.txt. Neither has a row in the header table — the same table whose own first line says it 'must stay in lock-step with the case statement below'. Counted: 16 case patterns, 14 api rows in the table.
push_allowlist_doc.missing_rows.consequence: A reader of that header believes the wrapper cannot publish the anchor receipt or the anchor history. It can, and does.
push_allowlist_doc.missing_rows.resolution: C1 Phase 1, when scripts/push-to-web-host.sh becomes a registry consumer and the table is rendered rather than typed. Fixing it here would mean editing the file, which Phase 0 forbids.
push_allowlist_doc.missing_rows.expires_when: the header table gains a row for either name, or either name leaves the case statement

derived._comment: Rendering instructions. Each output declares its own ORDER because the three target files list the same paths in three different orders, and the comment text that belongs to each entry differs per file. tests/publication-registry/ checks that every order list agrees with publications[] in both directions, so an entry cannot be added to one without the other.

header: # Dynamically-pushed feeds — written into the public web root's api/ and
# calendar/ by the validator-host-side push (scripts/push-to-web-host.sh) and the
# Xserver-side receive wrapper. Any rsync with --delete into a public tree
# MUST exclude these or the delete erases fresh feeds.
# Paths are relative to public/. Consumed by
# scripts/deploy/build-rsync-excludes.sh (single source of truth). Keep in
# lock-step with docs/DEPLOY_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md and the Xserver receive

comment_before: # Subdirectory feeds — whole-directory entries (like calendar/) because the
# member filenames are content-addressed / date-keyed and unbounded:
#   api/archive/       R18 per-anchor archives (anchor-source-<dag>.json,
#                      anchor-receipt-<tx>.json) — the pre-images that
#                      anchor-history.jsonl's archived_*_path fields point at.
#   api/peers-history/ daily gzipped validator-set snapshots, indexed by
#                      peers-history-index.json.
# Both are push-owned end to end (never git-tracked), so the deploy must
# neither deliver nor delete them.

trailer._comment: Lines that live inside the same .gitignore section but are NOT publications — cron-written alert-dedup state under logs/. They are carried verbatim so the rendered block covers the WHOLE section: with them, nothing can be inserted anywhere in the section without breaking byte equality. Without them the check would only cover the section's head and an entry appended at the bottom would slip through.
